user_input: According to the ablation study, which component contributes most to DocuSearch's grounding rate when removed, and which contributes least? (2609.01617)
retrieved_contexts:
Table[V](#S8.T5 "TABLE V ‣ VIII-D Ablation Study ‣ VIII Results and Analysis ‣ Hybrid Retrieval-Augmented Generation with Knowledge Graph Expansion, RRF Fusion, and Per-Chunk Grounded Evaluation for Enterprise Document Search") shows grounding rate when each
component is removed individually, holding everything
else constant.  
TABLE V: Ablation Study: Grounding Rate
| Configuration | Grounding Rate |
| --- | --- |
| Full DocuSearch | 89.6% |
| Without groundedness check | 74.3% |
| Without sufficiency scoring | 78.1% |
| Without neighbour expansion | 82.4% |
| Without cross-encoder reranking | 83.7% |
| Without KG expansion | 85.2% |
| Without vendor scoping | 86.1% |
  
Groundedness verification has the largest individual impact
at $15.3$ percentage points, followed by sufficiency scoring
at $11.5$ points. It is worth noting that even the
“smallest” contributors — vendor scoping at $3.5$ points
and KG expansion at $4.4$ points — add up meaningfully
in combination, indicating that no component is redundant.
response:
According to the ablation study, removing the **groundedness check (groundedness verification)** has the largest effect: grounding rate falls from **89.6% to 74.3%**, a decrease of **15.3 percentage points**.

Removing **vendor scoping** has the smallest effect: grounding rate falls to **86.1%**, a decrease of **3.5 percentage points**.【1】
